title: Spread and Rest Operators
objective: Use the ... operator to expand a value into individual elements, or to gather several arguments into one array.

sourceAlignment.title: JavaScript Crash Course
sourceAlignment.author: Nick Morgan
sourceAlignment.note: Original Code Forge chapter covering modern spread/rest syntax beyond the book's core coverage. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: The ... operator looks the same in every spot you use it, but it does one of two opposite things depending on where it appears: it either spreads a collection out into individual values, or gathers individual values into one collection.

As spread, ... expands an array or object into its individual elements. [...arr] copies an array into a brand-new one. [...arr1, ...arr2] merges two arrays into one. {...obj1, ...obj2} merges two objects into one, with obj2's properties overwriting obj1's if any keys collide.

As rest, ... does the opposite: it gathers any remaining function arguments into a single array. function total(first, ...rest) {} — calling total(1, 2, 3, 4) gives first the value 1, and rest becomes the array [2, 3, 4]. The rest parameter must be the last one in the function's parameter list.
explanation.rule: ... spreads a collection apart into individual values, or gathers individual values together into one array — spread expands, rest collects.

checks.question: const a = { x: 1, y: 2 }; const b = { y: 9, z: 3 }; const merged = { ...a, ...b }; — what is merged.y?

feedback.correct: Correct — b is spread after a, so b's y: 9 overwrites a's y: 2.
feedback.incorrect: When two spread objects share a key, the one spread LATER wins — here that's b, so y ends up 9.

assignment.title: Merge and Count
assignment.brief: Write mergeSettings(defaults, overrides) that returns a new object combining both, with overrides winning on shared keys. Then write countExtras(first, ...rest) that returns how many arguments came after the first one.
requirements: Define mergeSettings(defaults, overrides) using object spread, with overrides applied after defaults.
Define countExtras(first, ...rest) using a rest parameter.

requirementChecks.label: Defines countExtras() with a rest parameter

assignment.outputCheckLabel: mergeSettings applies overrides on top of defaults; countExtras counts the arguments after the first

hints: { ...defaults, ...overrides } spreads defaults first, then overrides on top, so overrides wins on shared keys.
function countExtras(first, ...rest) collects everything after first into the rest array automatically.
rest.length tells you how many extra arguments were passed.
countExtras('a', 'b', 'c', 'd') should return 3 — three arguments came after 'a'.
